concepts.name: AI learning systems
concepts.description: Systems that improve decisions or representations from data, interaction, or both.

concepts.name: Supervised learning
concepts.description: Learning a predictive mapping from labeled examples under an explicit loss.

concepts.name: Unsupervised learning
concepts.description: Discovering structure or representations without task labels.

concepts.name: Reinforcement learning
concepts.description: Learning sequential decisions from rewards while actions influence future data.

concepts.name: Probability reasoning
concepts.description: Reasoning about uncertainty, conditional probability, expectation, and dependence.

concepts.name: Empirical risk minimization
concepts.description: Selecting a hypothesis by minimizing average observed loss over a sample.

concepts.name: Generalization
concepts.description: Performance on future data drawn from the intended deployment process.

concepts.name: Data partitioning and validation
concepts.description: Designing train, validation, and test partitions that match the unit and chronology of deployment.

concepts.name: Data leakage
concepts.description: Information reaches model fitting or selection that would not be available at the prediction time being evaluated.

concepts.name: Bias and variance
concepts.description: Decomposing predictive error into systematic approximation and sensitivity to the sampled training set.

concepts.name: Regularization
concepts.description: Constraining effective model complexity to improve expected out-of-sample performance.

concepts.name: Linear predictive models
concepts.description: Models whose score is affine in their represented features, including logistic regression.

concepts.name: Feature scaling and geometry
concepts.description: How units and transformations change distance, penalties, and optimization geometry.

concepts.name: Gradient-based optimization
concepts.description: Iterative optimization driven by local derivatives, curvature, conditioning, and step-size choices.

concepts.name: Neural networks
concepts.description: Compositions of parameterized differentiable transformations that learn representations.

concepts.name: Backpropagation and computational graphs
concepts.description: Reverse-mode differentiation through a computational graph, including explicit gradient stops.

concepts.name: Representation learning
concepts.description: Learning features that make relevant structure usable by downstream tasks.

concepts.name: Attention
concepts.description: Content-dependent aggregation through query-key compatibility and value mixing.

concepts.name: Transformers
concepts.description: Sequence models built around attention, position information, residual paths, and feed-forward blocks.

concepts.name: Probabilistic calibration
concepts.description: Agreement between predicted probabilities and empirical event frequencies at the relevant granularity.

concepts.name: Ranking metrics
concepts.description: Threshold-independent evaluation of ordering, including ROC AUC and precision-recall behavior.

concepts.name: Decision thresholds and utility
concepts.description: Converting scores or probabilities into actions using costs, benefits, and capacity constraints.

concepts.name: Class imbalance
concepts.description: Learning and evaluation when outcome prevalence is highly unequal across classes.

concepts.name: Distribution shift
concepts.description: Changes between training and deployment distributions, including covariate, label, and concept shift.

concepts.name: Causal inference
concepts.description: Reasoning about interventions and counterfactual outcomes beyond observational association.

concepts.name: Generative modeling
concepts.description: Modeling a joint distribution or a data-generating process rather than only a decision rule.

concepts.name: Discriminative modeling
concepts.description: Modeling a conditional target distribution or decision boundary directly.

concepts.name: Dimensionality reduction
concepts.description: Mapping data to fewer coordinates while preserving a selected notion of structure.

concepts.name: Clustering
concepts.description: Grouping observations under explicit similarity, density, or graph assumptions.

concepts.name: Off-policy evaluation
concepts.description: Estimating a target policy's value from data generated by a different behavior policy.

concepts.name: Bellman reasoning and reward design
concepts.description: Relating immediate reward, discounted continuation value, and policy-preserving reward transformations.

concepts.name: Probabilistic knowledge tracing
concepts.description: Maintaining uncertain learner-skill state from noisy, multi-skill response evidence over time.

concepts.name: Information gain
concepts.description: Expected reduction in uncertainty from an observation or intervention.

concepts.name: Adaptive assessment
concepts.description: Selecting questions sequentially to balance diagnosis, learning, coverage, and operational constraints.

edges.rationale: Supervised learning is one major learning-system paradigm.
Unsupervised learning is one major learning-system paradigm.
Reinforcement learning is one major learning-system paradigm.
The paradigms differ primarily in whether task labels define the learning signal.
Supervised examples are usually exogenous, while an RL policy changes its future observations.
Expected loss and probabilistic prediction require conditional probability reasoning.
Empirical risk minimization is a core supervised-learning formulation.
Generalization analysis starts by distinguishing empirical from population risk.
A valid holdout design is needed to estimate deployment performance.
Leakage is diagnosed relative to split boundaries, prediction time, and unit of independence.
Leaked evaluation is not evidence of generalization.
Regularization is best understood as trading approximation bias for reduced estimation variance.
Bias and variance explain why low training error need not transfer.
Linear predictors are a foundational supervised model class.
Coordinate-wise penalties have meaning only relative to feature units.
Feature scales strongly affect curvature and optimization conditioning.
Most neural networks are fitted with gradient-based optimization.
Backpropagation questions assume an understanding of composed neural transformations.
Gradient flow determines which learned representations receive task signal.
Attention operates on and constructs learned representations.
Attention is the central token-mixing component of a transformer.
Calibration is a conditional-frequency property of probabilistic forecasts.
A score can order cases well while its numeric probabilities remain unreliable.
Cost-derived probability thresholds require trustworthy probability semantics.
Optimal action thresholds follow from comparing conditional expected costs.
Prevalence changes how ranking metrics, especially precision-recall summaries, should be interpreted.
Shift analysis refines what future distribution a generalization claim covers.
Shift types are distinguished through different factorizations of joint distributions.
Predictive association alone does not identify an intervention effect.
Joint and latent-variable models require probability factorization.
The primary contrast is joint or data-process modeling versus direct conditional prediction.
Discriminative prediction is a major supervised-learning approach.
Methods such as PCA learn structure without labels.
Clustering is a canonical unsupervised task.
Variance-based projections depend on the units of their coordinates.
Distance-based clusters depend on feature scale and geometry.
Bellman reasoning formalizes the sequential objective in reinforcement learning.
Off-policy evaluation assumes policies, trajectories, returns, and behavior data.
Importance ratios and support conditions are probabilistic concepts.
Knowledge tracing updates uncertain latent skill state from noisy observations.
A learner model should not interpret response likelihoods more literally than their calibration supports.
Expected information gain is one principled question-selection objective.
Adaptive selection consumes and updates the learner state maintained by knowledge tracing.
An adaptive policy must remain valid for new learners and avoid overfitting item history.

misconceptions.name: Leakage means only copying the target
misconceptions.description: Treats leakage as an explicit target column and misses proxies or features unavailable at prediction time.
misconceptions.remediation: Reconstruct the exact prediction timestamp and audit whether each value exists then.

misconceptions.name: More folds repair invalid split units
misconceptions.description: Assumes leave-one-out or many-fold validation fixes patient, group, or temporal dependence without changing the split unit.
misconceptions.remediation: Choose split units and chronology from deployment first; choose the number of folds second.

misconceptions.name: Unsupervised preprocessing cannot leak
misconceptions.description: Assumes scaling or representation fitting on all rows is harmless because labels are not used.
misconceptions.remediation: Fit every learned transformation inside each training partition and apply it unchanged to held-out data.

misconceptions.name: The test set may guide model selection
misconceptions.description: Uses test results to choose hyperparameters and still interprets the selected result as unbiased final evidence.
misconceptions.remediation: Use validation data for choices and reserve the test set for one locked evaluation.

misconceptions.name: More test-set trials reduce selection bias
misconceptions.description: Believes searching more configurations against the same test set makes the best score more reliable.
misconceptions.remediation: Study the winner's curse: maximizing noisy estimates increases optimism as the search grows.

misconceptions.name: Averaging restores a reused holdout
misconceptions.description: Assumes averaging scores removes the adaptivity created when test feedback influenced the workflow.
misconceptions.remediation: Track information flow, not just the final aggregation; adaptive reuse spends holdout validity.

misconceptions.name: L2 regularization is scale invariant
misconceptions.description: Extends the reparameterization invariance of an unpenalized linear score to a coordinate-wise L2 penalty.
misconceptions.remediation: Rewrite the penalty after a unit change and compare the feasible coefficient geometry.

misconceptions.name: Scaling affects speed but never the fitted model
misconceptions.description: Recognizes conditioning effects but ignores that regularization makes the optimization objective itself unit dependent.
misconceptions.remediation: Separate invariance of model predictions from invariance of the penalized objective.

misconceptions.name: One global lambda repairs any coordinate rescale
misconceptions.description: Assumes a scalar penalty multiplier can undo a rescaling applied to only one feature without affecting the others.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare per-coordinate penalty weights before and after rescaling.

misconceptions.name: Training error alone diagnoses variance
misconceptions.description: Uses a low training error to dismiss instability across plausible training samples.
misconceptions.remediation: Measure sensitivity across resamples; variance concerns fitted-model changes, not just in-sample fit.

misconceptions.name: More capacity reduces variance
misconceptions.description: Assumes a deeper or more flexible model smooths away fold-to-fold instability.
misconceptions.remediation: Contrast how capacity changes bias and sensitivity to sample-specific details.

misconceptions.name: The best single split is representative
misconceptions.description: Selects a favorable partition and treats cross-split variability as irrelevant noise.
misconceptions.remediation: Summarize performance across prespecified resamples and retain uncertainty in the estimate.

misconceptions.name: Probability 0.5 is the universal action threshold
misconceptions.description: Ignores asymmetric consequences and treats the conventional classification cutoff as a decision rule.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare the conditional expected cost of each action at probability p.

misconceptions.name: The decision threshold equals prevalence
misconceptions.description: Confuses the population base rate with the cost ratio at which two actions have equal expected loss.
misconceptions.remediation: Derive the threshold from costs, then separately examine how prevalence affects predicted probabilities.

misconceptions.name: F1 automatically represents real costs
misconceptions.description: Treats an unweighted harmonic mean of precision and recall as if it encoded a stated false-positive/false-negative utility.
misconceptions.remediation: Optimize the stated utility directly and use F1 only when its implicit tradeoff is intended.

misconceptions.name: High AUC implies calibrated probabilities
misconceptions.description: Infers accurate probability magnitudes from a metric that depends primarily on ordering.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare a monotonic score transformation: ranking can stay fixed while calibration changes.

misconceptions.name: Calibration determines ranking quality
misconceptions.description: Assumes a better reliability curve guarantees higher discrimination at every operating point.
misconceptions.remediation: Evaluate calibration and ranking as distinct axes of probabilistic performance.

misconceptions.name: Recalibration must change the ranking
misconceptions.description: Assumes correcting probability magnitudes necessarily retrains or reorders the underlying score.
misconceptions.remediation: Study monotone calibration maps, which can change probabilities while preserving order.

misconceptions.name: Stable class-conditionals mean no shift
misconceptions.description: Overlooks that changing class priors changes the joint and marginal deployment distributions.
misconceptions.remediation: Factor p(x,y) as p(x|y)p(y) and vary one factor at a time.

misconceptions.name: A prior change is covariate shift
misconceptions.description: Labels a change in p(y) with stable p(x|y) as covariate shift.
misconceptions.remediation: Contrast label shift with the covariate-shift assumption that p(y|x) remains stable.

misconceptions.name: A prior change is concept shift
misconceptions.description: Confuses changing outcome prevalence with a change in the conditional relationship from features to outcomes.
misconceptions.remediation: Identify exactly which conditional or marginal factor changed before naming the shift.

misconceptions.name: Predictive association implies intervention effect
misconceptions.description: Interprets a conditional association learned for prediction as the effect of setting a treatment.
misconceptions.remediation: Write separate observational and interventional queries: P(Y|T) versus P(Y|do(T)).

misconceptions.name: Any rich adjustment removes confounding
misconceptions.description: Assumes controlling many observed variables guarantees exchangeability, regardless of timing, colliders, or unmeasured causes.
misconceptions.remediation: Justify an adjustment set with a causal graph and explicit identification assumptions.

misconceptions.name: More observational data identify causality
misconceptions.description: Treats sampling precision as a remedy for structural non-identifiability.
misconceptions.remediation: Separate variance reduction from assumptions needed to identify an intervention effect.

misconceptions.name: A tiny learning rate fixes conditioning
misconceptions.description: Confuses stable steps with efficient progress when curvature differs greatly by direction.
misconceptions.remediation: Analyze convergence along the largest and smallest Hessian eigen-directions.

misconceptions.name: More iterations improve the condition number
misconceptions.description: Treats a geometric property of the objective as if it changes merely by running the same optimizer longer.
misconceptions.remediation: Distinguish modifying the objective geometry from traversing it for more steps.

misconceptions.name: Momentum guarantees perfect conditioning
misconceptions.description: Overstates acceleration and assumes momentum removes all sensitivity to curvature and scaling.
misconceptions.remediation: Treat momentum as an optimizer choice, not an algebraic transformation to condition number one.

misconceptions.name: Stop-gradient blocks downstream parameter updates
misconceptions.description: Assumes detaching an intermediate value prevents later layers from receiving gradients from their own operations.
misconceptions.remediation: Trace local derivatives backward edge by edge and mark only the detached edge as zero.

misconceptions.name: Forward use guarantees gradient flow
misconceptions.description: Assumes any parameter that influences a forward value must receive a gradient even across an explicit detach operation.
misconceptions.remediation: Separate forward dependence from differentiable backward connectivity.

misconceptions.name: Stop-gradient changes values but not derivatives
misconceptions.description: Reverses the operation: detach preserves the forward value precisely while replacing one backward derivative with zero.
misconceptions.remediation: Write the stop-gradient operator as identity in the forward pass and zero derivative in the backward pass.

misconceptions.name: Content attention inherently knows absolute position
misconceptions.description: Assumes global token interaction creates order information even when no positional signal is supplied.
misconceptions.remediation: Apply the same permutation to inputs and derive how Q, K, V, and the attention matrix transform.

misconceptions.name: Shared projections destroy permutation equivariance
misconceptions.description: Treats token-shared weight matrices as if they were tied to fixed sequence indices.
misconceptions.remediation: Track tensor shapes: feature projections act identically on every token row.

misconceptions.name: Symmetric pooling recovers order
misconceptions.description: Assumes mean or sum pooling can reconstruct ordering that the representation never encoded.
misconceptions.remediation: Prove that mean and sum are invariant under row permutations.

misconceptions.name: Full attention is linear in sequence length
misconceptions.description: Counts token projections but omits the pairwise query-key score matrix.
misconceptions.remediation: Write the L by L attention-score shape before estimating complexity.

misconceptions.name: Transformer parameter count scales with token count
misconceptions.description: Confuses activation sizes for a particular input with learned weights shared across positions.
misconceptions.remediation: List parameter matrices separately from per-example activations.

misconceptions.name: Attention is quadratic only during training
misconceptions.description: Assumes removing backward storage changes the pairwise forward computation into a linear one.
misconceptions.remediation: Distinguish forward asymptotic complexity from the additional constants and storage of backpropagation.

misconceptions.name: Generative means neural sample synthesis
misconceptions.description: Defines generative models by modern media generation rather than by the modeled distribution.
misconceptions.remediation: Classify models by whether they represent a joint/data distribution or only a conditional decision.

misconceptions.name: Discriminative models cannot output probabilities
misconceptions.description: Confuses direct conditional modeling with deterministic classification.
misconceptions.remediation: Use logistic regression as a counterexample that directly models P(Y|X).

misconceptions.name: Joint modeling is assumption free
misconceptions.description: Assumes modeling more of the data distribution guarantees dominance without additional modeling commitments.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare what each approach must estimate and how misspecification affects its sample tradeoff.

misconceptions.name: PCA finds the most predictive directions
misconceptions.description: Equates high marginal feature variance with separation of a downstream label.
misconceptions.remediation: Contrast PCA's unlabeled variance objective with a supervised prediction objective.

misconceptions.name: PCA is invariant to feature units
misconceptions.description: Ignores that covariance eigenvectors change when one coordinate is rescaled.
misconceptions.remediation: Compute a two-feature covariance matrix before and after changing one unit.

misconceptions.name: More retained components always improve generalization
misconceptions.description: Assumes retaining information cannot increase variance or reintroduce noise for a downstream learner.
misconceptions.remediation: Select representation dimension using held-out downstream performance, not reconstruction alone.

misconceptions.name: K-means is density based
misconceptions.description: Assumes centroid assignment discovers arbitrarily shaped or variable-density regions.
misconceptions.remediation: Relate the k-means objective to Voronoi cells and within-cluster squared Euclidean distance.

misconceptions.name: An internal metric proves true clusters
misconceptions.description: Treats a high silhouette score under one geometry as evidence of uniquely real semantic groups.
misconceptions.remediation: Validate stability, sensitivity, and external usefulness while acknowledging clustering assumptions.

misconceptions.name: Feature scale does not affect k-means
misconceptions.description: Ignores that rescaling a coordinate changes squared Euclidean distances and therefore the objective.
misconceptions.remediation: Expand the distance formula and inspect each coordinate's contribution after rescaling.

misconceptions.name: Importance sampling works without support
misconceptions.description: Assumes a zero behavior probability can be corrected by weighting rather than making the target action unobserved.
misconceptions.remediation: Write the target-to-behavior likelihood ratio and inspect division by zero.

misconceptions.name: A learned dynamics model eliminates coverage needs
misconceptions.description: Treats model-based extrapolation into unsupported actions as identified fact rather than an assumption-sensitive estimate.
misconceptions.remediation: Separate statistical identification from extrapolation supplied by a model class.

misconceptions.name: Logged returns transfer directly across policies
misconceptions.description: Ignores that a different policy changes action choices, state visitation, and subsequent rewards.
misconceptions.remediation: Trace how the policy changes the trajectory distribution even in the same environment.

misconceptions.name: Any positive progress reward preserves the policy
misconceptions.description: Assumes locally helpful dense rewards cannot create cycles or alter the ranking of long-term returns.
misconceptions.remediation: Check whether the shaping reward telescopes as a discounted potential difference.

misconceptions.name: Discount may be omitted from potential shaping
misconceptions.description: Uses an undiscounted potential difference inside a discounted MDP, breaking the telescoping policy-invariance argument.
misconceptions.remediation: Expand the discounted return and verify cancellation requires gamma times the next potential.

misconceptions.name: Preserving terminal order makes shaping safe
misconceptions.description: Ignores path length, cycles, and intermediate reward accumulation when comparing policies.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare full discounted trajectory returns, not only terminal-state rankings.

misconceptions.name: Lower training loss guarantees lower test loss
misconceptions.description: Transfers the monotonic empirical-risk property of nested model classes to unknown population risk.
misconceptions.remediation: Separate optimization error, empirical risk, and the estimation gap.

misconceptions.name: ERM directly minimizes population risk
misconceptions.description: Treats a sample average as if it were the inaccessible deployment expectation.
misconceptions.remediation: Write empirical and expected risk as distinct quantities indexed by the selected hypothesis.

misconceptions.name: A validation set removes complexity concerns
misconceptions.description: Assumes finite validation data permit unlimited adaptive search without selection variance or overfitting.
misconceptions.remediation: Treat model selection itself as an adaptive statistical procedure with finite evidence.

misconceptions.name: One wrong response disproves every required skill
misconceptions.description: Deterministically marks all linked concepts unmastered despite slips and ambiguity in which skill caused failure.
misconceptions.remediation: Update a posterior through the response likelihood instead of assigning a hard state.

misconceptions.name: The highest-weight skill is the unique failure cause
misconceptions.description: Interprets content weights as a deterministic causal label for a multi-skill response.
misconceptions.remediation: Marginalize over plausible latent skill states and retain uncertainty about attribution.

misconceptions.name: Ambiguous multi-skill evidence is useless
misconceptions.description: Discards a response because it does not isolate one concept, rather than making a smaller joint posterior update.
misconceptions.remediation: Use a multi-skill observation model: ambiguous evidence can still shift several hypotheses probabilistically.

misconceptions.name: The hardest item is always most informative
misconceptions.description: Ignores the learner's current ability and the nearly deterministic response expected on an excessively hard item.
misconceptions.remediation: Plot expected information across item difficulty relative to the current learner posterior.

misconceptions.name: Mastery uncertainty is the only selection goal
misconceptions.description: Selects solely by a 0.5 mastery probability while ignoring item discrimination, prerequisites, learning value, and coverage.
misconceptions.remediation: Compute expected posterior change per candidate and add explicit pedagogical and content constraints.

misconceptions.name: Greedy information gain needs no constraints
misconceptions.description: Assumes repeatedly selecting one diagnostic item family is acceptable despite exposure, fatigue, coverage, and instructional goals.
misconceptions.remediation: Optimize information or learning value under content balancing and exposure constraints.

misconceptions.name: K-means centroids are robust to outliers
misconceptions.description: Treats the squared-distance centroid objective as insensitive to a small number of extreme observations.
misconceptions.remediation: Expand the squared-distance contribution of an extreme point and compare robust clustering objectives.

misconceptions.name: Cluster labels have fixed identity
misconceptions.description: Compares numeric cluster labels across fits without first aligning the arbitrary permutations of those labels.
misconceptions.remediation: Align partitions by membership or use a label-permutation-invariant agreement measure.

misconceptions.name: Adding clusters resolves instability
misconceptions.description: Assumes increasing k repairs sensitivity to sampling, initialization, or weak separation without examining the fitted partitions.
misconceptions.remediation: Measure resampling stability and inspect whether the added groups persist and remain useful.

misconceptions.name: PCA variance fractions use standard deviations
misconceptions.description: Adds square roots of covariance eigenvalues when computing explained variance instead of adding the eigenvalues themselves.
misconceptions.remediation: Recall that covariance eigenvalues are variances along principal directions.

misconceptions.name: Principal components select original features
misconceptions.description: Interprets each principal component as one retained input column rather than a direction formed from feature loadings.
misconceptions.remediation: Write a component score explicitly as a weighted linear combination of centered inputs.

misconceptions.name: A PCA loading sign has intrinsic meaning
misconceptions.description: Treats the sign of an eigenvector as identified even though multiplying the full direction by negative one gives the same component axis.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare an eigenvector with its negation and distinguish relative loading signs from global orientation.

misconceptions.name: Orthogonal components are statistically independent
misconceptions.description: Equates zero covariance of PCA scores with statistical independence without distributional assumptions such as joint Gaussianity.
misconceptions.remediation: Separate geometric orthogonality and zero covariance from the stronger factorization required by independence.

misconceptions.name: Logistic probability is linear in the features
misconceptions.description: Confuses a linear log-odds score with a probability that changes linearly across the feature space.
misconceptions.remediation: Apply the sigmoid to the affine score and distinguish the score surface from the probability surface.

misconceptions.name: Changing a logistic threshold leaves the boundary fixed
misconceptions.description: Assumes a probability threshold has no effect on the intercept level defining the classifier's decision surface.
misconceptions.remediation: Convert the probability threshold to a log-odds threshold and solve for the new boundary.

misconceptions.name: A discriminative model specifies the feature distribution
misconceptions.description: Treats a conditional model for labels given features as a complete probability model for features and labels jointly.
misconceptions.remediation: Factor a joint distribution and identify which factors are and are not supplied by a conditional classifier.

misconceptions.name: Classification requires an explicit joint model
misconceptions.description: Assumes prediction of labels given observed features requires separately modeling how the features were generated.
misconceptions.remediation: Use the learned conditional probabilities directly for a decision under a stated loss.

misconceptions.name: Class weights change optimization speed but not the target
misconceptions.description: Ignores that class-dependent weights alter the population objective and therefore the probability represented by its optimum.
misconceptions.remediation: Derive the pointwise minimizer of weighted log loss and compare it with the unweighted posterior.

misconceptions.name: Weighted-loss probabilities retain population calibration
misconceptions.description: Reads scores learned under class-weighted log loss as unadjusted event probabilities in the deployment population.
misconceptions.remediation: Account for the weighting-induced odds shift or recalibrate on representative held-out data.

misconceptions.name: ERM is independent of the loss function
misconceptions.description: Assumes the same fitted hypothesis minimizes empirical risk after changing the pointwise loss.
misconceptions.remediation: Solve a simple constant-prediction problem under squared and absolute loss.

misconceptions.name: Zero-one loss and log loss have the same empirical optimizer
misconceptions.description: Conflates agreement in some decision boundaries with identity of objectives and fitted probability scores.
misconceptions.remediation: Write both empirical objectives and identify what each rewards among probability predictions.

misconceptions.name: Regularization contributes extra observed examples
misconceptions.description: Treats a parameter penalty as additional empirical evidence rather than an explicit preference in the optimization objective.
misconceptions.remediation: Separate the data-fit sum from the penalty and state the information source represented by each term.

misconceptions.name: A penalty leaves the empirical minimizer unchanged
misconceptions.description: Assumes adding a nonconstant regularization term preserves the minimizer of the unpenalized sample loss.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare first-order conditions before and after adding the penalty.

misconceptions.name: Standardization is purely numerical
misconceptions.description: Ignores that scaling coordinates changes the metric and relative feature influence used by distance-based algorithms.
misconceptions.remediation: Write the Euclidean distance before and after scaling one coordinate.

misconceptions.name: Changing measurement units changes information content
misconceptions.description: Interprets an invertible unit conversion as adding or removing predictive information from the observations.
misconceptions.remediation: Distinguish an invertible representation change from its effect on a particular algorithm or prior.

misconceptions.name: Coefficients are invariant to feature units
misconceptions.description: Expects a regression coefficient to keep the same numerical value when its corresponding feature is rescaled.
misconceptions.remediation: Preserve the linear predictor algebraically after multiplying a feature by a constant.

misconceptions.name: Equivalent predictions imply equivalent coefficient penalties
misconceptions.description: Assumes a reparameterization that preserves fitted values also preserves an L1 or L2 norm on the coefficients.
misconceptions.remediation: Substitute the rescaled coefficient into the chosen penalty and compare magnitudes.

misconceptions.name: A unit conversion changes tree partitions
misconceptions.description: Assumes positive monotone rescaling changes the ordering of candidate split points and therefore the fitted partition of a standard decision tree.
misconceptions.remediation: Track observation order and translated thresholds under a positive affine feature transformation.

misconceptions.name: A linear model forbids nonlinear feature maps
misconceptions.description: Defines linearity by the raw input shape rather than by linearity in the fitted coefficients.
misconceptions.remediation: Express polynomial regression as an inner product between coefficients and transformed features.

misconceptions.name: A linear model implies a linear probability
misconceptions.description: Transfers linearity of a score or parameterization to the response scale after a nonlinear link function.
misconceptions.remediation: Name the scale on which additivity holds and then apply the response link.

misconceptions.name: Basis expansion makes the parameters nonlinear
misconceptions.description: Confuses nonlinear transformations of inputs with nonlinear dependence on the unknown coefficients.
misconceptions.remediation: Hold the transformed design matrix fixed and inspect how coefficients enter the prediction.

misconceptions.name: Multicollinearity invalidates all predictions
misconceptions.description: Equates uncertainty in individual coefficients with unusable fitted values throughout the observed predictor region.
misconceptions.remediation: Separate identifiable linear combinations used for prediction from unstable attribution to individual columns.

misconceptions.name: High fit quality identifies individual coefficients
misconceptions.description: Treats a strong aggregate fit as evidence that correlated predictors have separately determined effects.
misconceptions.remediation: Examine the coefficient covariance or equivalent fits along a nearly collinear direction.

misconceptions.name: Linearity validates extrapolation
misconceptions.description: Assumes a simple functional form provides empirical support beyond the range where predictor-response behavior was observed.
misconceptions.remediation: Distinguish the model's algebraic extension from evidence that the relationship persists outside support.

misconceptions.name: Sensitivity equals positive predictive value
misconceptions.description: Reverses the conditioning direction between the probability of a positive test given disease and disease given a positive test.
misconceptions.remediation: Write each conditional probability with its event after the conditioning bar and apply Bayes' rule.

misconceptions.name: A positive test makes the base rate irrelevant
misconceptions.description: Updates from test accuracy without accounting for how many diseased and nondiseased cases enter the tested population.
misconceptions.remediation: Construct expected counts from prevalence, sensitivity, and false-positive rate.

misconceptions.name: False-positive rate is the posterior error rate
misconceptions.description: Confuses the fraction of nondiseased cases testing positive with the fraction of positive tests coming from nondiseased cases.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare the denominators of the two rates in a contingency table.

misconceptions.name: Conditional independence implies marginal independence
misconceptions.description: Drops the conditioning variable and assumes a factorization persists after mixing across its values.
misconceptions.remediation: Marginalize a conditionally independent model over a shared latent cause and inspect the resulting dependence.

misconceptions.name: Expectation commutes with nonlinear functions
misconceptions.description: Substitutes the mean into a nonlinear transformation as if linearity of expectation applied to the transformation itself.
misconceptions.remediation: Evaluate both quantities for a two-point random variable and compare.

misconceptions.name: Reinforcement learning is supervised learning on rewards
misconceptions.description: Treats observed rewards as labels for isolated actions while ignoring delayed consequences and policy-dependent data.
misconceptions.remediation: Write the return following an action and track how the action changes future states and observations.

misconceptions.name: Actions do not change future data
misconceptions.description: Assumes the learner receives an externally fixed dataset even when its choices affect state transitions and later experience.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare passive prediction data with trajectories generated under two different policies.

misconceptions.name: A greedy policy eventually explores on its own
misconceptions.description: Assumes elapsed time supplies evidence about actions that the current policy stops selecting.
misconceptions.remediation: Track action counts after an unlucky initial estimate under a strictly greedy selection rule.

misconceptions.name: Uniform random exploration is intrinsically optimal
misconceptions.description: Treats undirected random action choice as the best information strategy without considering uncertainty, regret, or state reachability.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare random exploration with uncertainty-aware or optimism-based exploration for the stated objective.

misconceptions.name: Discounting starts with the immediate reward
misconceptions.description: Multiplies the current reward by gamma rather than assigning exponent zero to the reward received at the current step.
misconceptions.remediation: Index each reward by its temporal offset in the return definition.

misconceptions.name: Discount has no role beyond random termination
misconceptions.description: Treats one useful interpretation of gamma as its complete meaning and ignores its direct weighting of delayed rewards.
misconceptions.remediation: Compute discounted returns for two reward timings even in a fixed finite horizon.

misconceptions.name: Changing a threshold repairs probability semantics
misconceptions.description: Assumes selecting a different classification cutoff converts systematically shifted scores back into calibrated population probabilities.
misconceptions.remediation: Separate ranking and classification decisions from calibration of the reported numeric probabilities.

misconceptions.name: Squared loss targets the sample median
misconceptions.description: Transfers the robust constant-predictor solution for absolute loss to a squared-error objective.
misconceptions.remediation: Differentiate the sum of squared residuals with respect to a constant prediction.

misconceptions.name: Absolute loss targets the sample mean
misconceptions.description: Assumes the balancing condition for squared residuals also minimizes the sum of absolute residual magnitudes.
misconceptions.remediation: Inspect the slope of absolute loss on either side of the ordered sample values.

misconceptions.name: All model families require standardization
misconceptions.description: Treats scale sensitivity as a universal property rather than one determined by an algorithm's geometry, parameterization, and optimization.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare order-based tree splits with Euclidean distance and coefficient-penalty calculations.

misconceptions.name: Dropping a correlated feature preserves coefficient interpretation
misconceptions.description: Assumes removing one correlated predictor leaves the remaining coefficient's estimand unchanged despite reallocation of shared association.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare partial-regression interpretations before and after removing a correlated covariate.

misconceptions.name: Linear predictions are clipped to the training response range
misconceptions.description: Assumes the fitted affine equation stops or saturates when a predictor leaves its observed range.
misconceptions.remediation: Evaluate the fitted equation at a predictor value outside the training support.

misconceptions.name: Low training error validates extrapolation
misconceptions.description: Uses in-range fit quality as direct evidence for the response relationship in an unobserved predictor region.
misconceptions.remediation: Identify which observations, assumptions, or domain constraints support behavior beyond the sample range.

misconceptions.name: A shared cause does not induce marginal dependence
misconceptions.description: Assumes variables remain unrelated after mixing over a latent cause that changes both of their probabilities.
misconceptions.remediation: Marginalize over the shared cause and compare a joint probability with the product of its marginals.

misconceptions.name: Conditional independence means identical test behavior
misconceptions.description: Confuses factorization of a conditional joint distribution with equality of the variables' sensitivities and false-positive rates.
misconceptions.remediation: Write separate conditional Bernoulli parameters while preserving the conditional factorization.

misconceptions.name: The expected value is the most likely outcome
misconceptions.description: Treats a distributional average as a mode or even as a value that the random variable can attain.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare the mean, support, and mode of a symmetric two-point distribution.

misconceptions.name: Mean and variance determine all nonlinear expectations
misconceptions.description: Assumes the first two moments determine expectations of arbitrary nonlinear functions across different distributions.
misconceptions.remediation: Construct two distributions with matching first two moments but different higher-order moments.

misconceptions.name: Delayed reward belongs entirely to the last action
misconceptions.description: Assigns a delayed outcome to the most recent choice without considering earlier actions that changed the state trajectory.
misconceptions.remediation: Trace return and credit across the state-action sequence leading to the delayed outcome.

misconceptions.name: Reward prediction establishes a new policy's value
misconceptions.description: Assumes accurate one-step reward prediction on logged actions identifies outcomes under actions and states poorly covered by the logging policy.
misconceptions.remediation: Audit action support, transition effects, and the policy mismatch before estimating counterfactual return.

misconceptions.name: Reward order does not affect discounted return
misconceptions.description: Treats discounted return as a function of the reward multiset while ignoring when each reward arrives.
misconceptions.remediation: Swap two rewards at different delays and recompute their gamma exponents.

misconceptions.name: Supervised learning means classification
misconceptions.description: Restricts supervised learning to discrete class labels and excludes regression with observed numeric targets.
misconceptions.remediation: Identify the observed target and loss in both a classification task and a regression task.

misconceptions.name: Labeled training data guarantee generalization
misconceptions.description: Treats access to labels and low training loss as sufficient evidence of performance on future deployment examples.
misconceptions.remediation: Separate the supervised training signal from held-out evidence under the intended deployment process.

misconceptions.name: Any observed target defines the deployment goal
misconceptions.description: Assumes a conveniently recorded label is automatically the outcome that the deployed decision should optimize.
misconceptions.remediation: State the deployment decision and verify that the training target and loss represent its desired outcome.

misconceptions.name: Unsupervised learning has no objective
misconceptions.description: Confuses absence of task labels with absence of an explicit reconstruction, density, contrastive, or clustering objective.
misconceptions.remediation: Write the criterion optimized by an unlabeled-data method and distinguish it from an external task label.

misconceptions.name: Clusters are observed ground truth
misconceptions.description: Treats groups returned by an unsupervised algorithm as uniquely correct labels rather than consequences of a chosen objective and representation.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare clusterings produced by two defensible similarity choices and evaluate them against the intended use.

misconceptions.name: Reconstruction guarantees downstream usefulness
misconceptions.description: Assumes preserving input detail under an unsupervised objective necessarily preserves the information needed by a later task.
misconceptions.remediation: Evaluate the learned representation on held-out downstream outcomes rather than inferring utility from reconstruction alone.

misconceptions.name: Training fit is generalization
misconceptions.description: Uses performance on fitted examples as direct evidence of performance on new draws from the deployment process.
misconceptions.remediation: Estimate performance on untouched examples sampled with the same units and chronology as deployment.

misconceptions.name: More source data repair distribution mismatch
misconceptions.description: Assumes an arbitrarily large sample from the wrong population identifies performance in a different deployment distribution.
misconceptions.remediation: Distinguish sampling uncertainty within a distribution from bias caused by a mismatch between source and target distributions.

misconceptions.name: Average performance guarantees subgroup performance
misconceptions.description: Infers reliable behavior for every deployment subgroup from a satisfactory aggregate test metric.
misconceptions.remediation: Report uncertainty and performance for decision-relevant subgroups in addition to the deployment-weighted aggregate.

misconceptions.name: Depth alone creates nonlinear expressivity
misconceptions.description: Assumes stacking affine layers without nonlinear activations yields functions beyond a single affine transformation.
misconceptions.remediation: Compose two affine maps algebraically and identify the activation that prevents their collapse.

misconceptions.name: Universal approximation guarantees successful training
misconceptions.description: Treats an existence result for representable functions as a guarantee that finite data and an optimizer will find a useful solution.
misconceptions.remediation: Separate representational capacity from optimization, sample efficiency, and out-of-sample validation.

misconceptions.name: Hidden units have fixed human meanings
misconceptions.description: Assumes each learned coordinate has an intrinsic, uniquely identifiable semantic interpretation across equivalent parameterizations.
misconceptions.remediation: Apply a permutation of hidden units and the inverse permutation to the next layer while observing unchanged predictions.

misconceptions.name: The most lossless representation is always best
misconceptions.description: Ranks representations only by retained input detail even when nuisance variation harms the downstream task.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare representations using held-out task utility and robustness to known nuisance changes.

misconceptions.name: Representation dimension determines utility
misconceptions.description: Infers downstream usefulness solely from the number of coordinates rather than the information and invariances they encode.
misconceptions.remediation: Hold dimension fixed while changing the learned objective, then compare downstream separability and robustness.

misconceptions.name: Pretraining guarantees transfer
misconceptions.description: Assumes success on a source pretraining objective necessarily improves every target task and domain.
misconceptions.remediation: Measure target-task performance under a deployment-aligned split and compare frozen, fine-tuned, and baseline representations.

misconceptions.name: Transformers are inherently bidirectional
misconceptions.description: Treats the architecture name as fixing information flow even though attention masks determine which token positions are visible.
misconceptions.remediation: Draw the allowed attention edges for causal, bidirectional, and encoder-decoder masks.

misconceptions.name: Position-wise feed-forward layers mix tokens
misconceptions.description: Attributes cross-token communication to the feed-forward sublayer even though its weights are applied independently at each position.
misconceptions.remediation: Track the sequence and feature axes through attention and the position-wise feed-forward network.

misconceptions.name: Residual paths make sublayer order irrelevant
misconceptions.description: Assumes skip connections make attention, normalization, and feed-forward ordering interchangeable.
misconceptions.remediation: Write the computations for two sublayer orders and identify the different inputs seen by each nonlinear transformation.

misconceptions.name: ROC and precision-recall share prevalence invariance
misconceptions.description: Assumes precision-recall values are unchanged by class prevalence just because ROC rates condition within each class.
misconceptions.remediation: Hold sensitivity and false-positive rate fixed while recomputing precision under two prevalences.

misconceptions.name: Accuracy is sufficient under class imbalance
misconceptions.description: Treats a high aggregate accuracy as informative even when a majority-class rule ignores the rare outcome of interest.
misconceptions.remediation: Inspect the confusion matrix and decision costs rather than relying on the aggregate correct fraction.

misconceptions.name: Class resampling preserves population probabilities
misconceptions.description: Reads probabilities learned after changing class proportions as calibrated deployment probabilities without correction or representative validation.
misconceptions.remediation: Account for the sampling-induced odds shift or recalibrate on a representative held-out sample.

misconceptions.name: Information gain is the surprise of one outcome
misconceptions.description: Confuses the expected reduction in uncertainty before observing a result with the surprise of the particular result obtained.
misconceptions.remediation: Average posterior entropy over all possible outcomes before subtracting it from prior entropy.

misconceptions.name: Correlated evidence adds full independent information
misconceptions.description: Counts repeated or shared-family observations as independent reductions in uncertainty despite their common error source.
misconceptions.remediation: Condition the second observation on the first and measure only its remaining mutual information.

misconceptions.name: High outcome entropy guarantees useful information
misconceptions.description: Assumes an unpredictable measurement is informative about the target even when it is statistically independent noise.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare marginal outcome entropy with conditional entropy given the target hypothesis.

misconceptions.name: Duplicates across splits are independent evidence
misconceptions.description: Treats near-duplicate records in training and evaluation partitions as separate evidence despite shared content or entity identity.
misconceptions.remediation: Deduplicate or group related records before splitting and evaluate on genuinely unseen units.

misconceptions.name: Resampling variation is only metric noise
misconceptions.description: Dismisses large changes in fitted predictions across plausible training samples as irrelevant evaluation noise rather than estimator variance.
misconceptions.remediation: Compare fitted functions or predictions across resampled training sets, not only uncertainty in a reported average.

misconceptions.name: Stronger regularization always improves generalization
misconceptions.description: Assumes increasing a penalty monotonically improves held-out performance and cannot introduce harmful bias or underfitting.
misconceptions.remediation: Tune regularization on untouched validation data and inspect both training and validation error across strengths.

misconceptions.name: Global calibration implies subgroup calibration
misconceptions.description: Infers calibrated probabilities in every relevant subgroup from calibration after pooling groups with different error patterns.
misconceptions.remediation: Check reliability within prespecified decision-relevant groups and report uncertainty from limited samples.

misconceptions.name: A ranking metric determines the action threshold
misconceptions.description: Assumes ROC AUC or another ordering summary identifies the probability cutoff that maximizes deployment utility.
misconceptions.remediation: Combine calibrated probabilities with explicit costs, benefits, and capacity constraints to choose an action rule.

misconceptions.name: A threshold survives cost and prevalence changes
misconceptions.description: Reuses a previously optimized cutoff after deployment probabilities or action consequences change without re-evaluation.
misconceptions.remediation: Recompute expected utility under the new probability calibration, costs, and operating constraints.

misconceptions.name: Higher generative likelihood guarantees better decisions
misconceptions.description: Assumes a model with higher overall data likelihood must perform better on every conditional prediction or utility-weighted action.
misconceptions.remediation: Evaluate the conditional quantity and decision utility directly in addition to the joint-model likelihood.

misconceptions.name: A stable feature marginal rules out shift
misconceptions.description: Concludes that deployment is unchanged from a stable p(x) even when the conditional outcome mechanism p(y|x) has changed.
misconceptions.remediation: Audit the joint factorization and test conditional outcome behavior rather than checking feature marginals alone.

misconceptions.name: Any conditional change is label shift
misconceptions.description: Calls a change in p(y|x) label shift even though label shift assumes stable class-conditional features and a changed class prior.
misconceptions.remediation: State which factor in p(x,y) is assumed stable before naming the shift.

misconceptions.name: Covariate shift changes the label mechanism
misconceptions.description: Defines covariate shift as a change in p(y|x) rather than a change in p(x) with a stable conditional outcome relationship.
misconceptions.remediation: Contrast p_source(x) with p_target(x) while holding p(y|x) fixed in the covariate-shift factorization.

sources.title: AI foundations bundle schema conventions
sources.notes: Edges point from a prerequisite, component, or contrasted concept to the downstream or paired concept. Question difficulty is an expert-prior IRT b value; discrimination is an expert-prior IRT a value; guess_rate and slip_rate are probabilities. Concept weights sum to 1. Correct options have a null misconception_id; every distractor names exactly one misconception. These priors require empirical recalibration.
